instruction: Export the active browser tabs to PDF format and save them in /home/user/Downloads/Papers, naming each file after the corresponding article title.

metadata.explanation: Task requires exporting 2 Chrome tabs to PDF files in /home/user/Downloads/Papers directory. The evaluator checks if 2 PDFs exist and their filenames contain keywords from the article titles ('agent' and 'human').

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly extracts PDF filenames from the target directory using bash find command
Metric correctly checks that exactly 2 PDFs exist in the directory
Metric correctly uses case-insensitive keyword matching to verify filename content
Expected values are semantically appropriate - keywords 'agent' and 'human' are derived from article URLs
Postconfig appropriately installs PyMuPDF for potential PDF content verification

ISSUE: Metric verification is incomplete - it only checks if keywords appear anywhere in filenames, not that each PDF uniquely corresponds to one article. The current logic would incorrectly pass if both keywords appear in a single filename (e.g., 'agent-human.pdf' + 'random.pdf')
ISSUE: Metric doesn't enforce one-to-one mapping between PDFs and articles as implied by instruction 'naming each file after the corresponding article title'
MINOR: The partial credit scoring (score += 1.0/len(required_keywords)) doesn't account for the mapping requirement between keywords and distinct files
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Improve metric to ensure each required keyword appears in a DIFFERENT PDF filename (one-to-one mapping)
Consider tracking which keywords are found in which files to prevent duplicate keywords in one file from counting
Alternative approach: Check that each PDF filename contains exactly one of the required keywords, ensuring 2 distinct files for 2 articles
